1384: Dyskerin detaches the base of a uridine, rotates it and reattaches it through a carbon: this is a pseudouridine. No atom is added or lost.
1385: Isomerisation: the N1–C1′ bond is broken, the uracil rotates, and a carbon–carbon C5–C1′ bond forms. The freed nitrogen 1 offers one more hydrogen-bond donor: the helix is stiffened. The target uridine sits in the pocket of the guide RNA, 14 to 16 nucleotides upstream of box H or ACA; an aspartate of dyskerin catalyses.

1388: In the processome, an enzyme cuts the pre-rRNA between the 5′ETS and 18S: the 5′ end of the future 18S is formed.
1389: UTP24 (PIN domain) hydrolyses the phosphodiester bond at site 1, then in ITS1; the cut leaves a 3′-OH and a 5′-phosphate. The U3 snoRNP, paired with the 5′ETS and 18S, holds the pre-rRNA in place and delays folding of the central pseudoknot. RNase MRP cuts at site 2 of ITS1 and separates the small and large subunit pathways.
1390: Which snoRNP guides the early cleavages of 18S?
1392: The removed pieces are destroyed, and some ends are trimmed nucleotide by nucleotide, by the exosome.
1393: Hydrolytic 3′→5′ exonucleases: each cut releases a nucleoside 5′-monophosphate. The RNA is unwound by the helicase MTR4 then threaded through the channel of the nine-subunit core, inactive by itself, down to DIS3; EXOSC10 acts at the surface. The exosome shapes the 3′ end of 5.8S, degrades the 5′ETS and removes defective pre-rRNAs. On the 5′ side, XRN2 does the trimming.
